subject: Chronicle: who/when export specification and sample request
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@finserv.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Chroncile: who/when export specification and sample request

Hi Emma — great speaking earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on the audit/log bundle you asked for.

Summary of ask (as I heard it):
- Who accessed model outputs (service account or user id) and when (UTC timestamps)
- Full event types for read/access operations across inference endpoints for the last 12 months (you said priority is last 3–6 months)
- Export format that works for you: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON) or CSV with canonical headers
- Pseudonymization: remove or hash raw prompts; leave metadata for repro

Clarifying Qs for you:
- Retention window you need us to export (you mentioned 7 years in passing — please confirm)
- Preferred delivery channel: secure S3 presigned link, encrypted SFTP drop, or a GCS/SFTP partner?
- Any specific column names or ticket reference formats procurement needs in the header?

What we can deliver quickly:
- One-month sample (NDJSON + CSV header) within 5 business days once format approved
- Full scoped export (up to 12 months) estimated 10–15 business days depending on size and residency requirements

I’ve looped in Rishi for schema and delivery details and Monica for the procurement/data-transfer checklist. If this looks right I’ll prepare a one-month sample and a short delivery checklist for your procurement team.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachment: FinServ_request_form.pdf (submitted by FinServ on call)
From: Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@finserv.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinServ Security <security@finserv.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 11:03:42 -0400
Subject: Re: Chroncile: who/when export specification and sample request

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the recap. A few specifics from our side:

1) Retention window: we need access records covering 24 months for the initial review; long-term retention policy will be handled by our legal team but for the proof we’d like 24 months exported.
2) Required fields (minimum): event_id, timestamp_utc, model_name, endpoint_id, action_type (inference_request / inference_response / cache_hit), principal_type (user, service), principal_id (hashed if PII), request_size_tokens, response_size_tokens, region, request_id
3) PII constraints: we cannot receive raw user prompts. If you include prompt metadata please pseudonymize or hash with a salt you provide to our security team separately.
4) Delivery: secure S3 presigned link preferred. We will give you a short-term upload bucket if that is easier.
5) Chain of custody: procurement will need a checklist that includes who exported, hash of file delivered, and time of upload. We may also request a signed DPA addendum before full export.

Please send the one-month sample (CSV & NDJSON if possible) to the presigned link you prefer. Will loop in procurement after we review sample.

—Emma
Emma Lawson
Director, Information Security | FinServ Financial
emma.lawson@finserv.com

Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 08:34:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Chroncile: who/when export specification and sample request

Emma — quick tech note from our infra side. Thanks for the clear field list. A few implementation points and constraints so procurement can plan bandwidth: 

- Schema: we can produce both NDJSON (recommended for large exports) and a compressed CSV. Attached is a one-month sample CSV we will use as the canonical header set (who_when_sample.csv) and a short schema doc (redwood_log_schema.md).
- PII handling: we will never export raw prompts. For principal_id we can provide an HMAC-SHA256 hash using a customer-specific salt. If you want reversible pseudonymization, we’ll need an executed DPA and KMS arrangement (we can discuss).
- Timestamps: all events normalized to UTC; we will include original timezone offset if present.
- Size: estimate ~1.2GB per month for high-traffic endpoints (approx 60M events). If you need 24 months, expect a multi-GB export — we recommend incremental deliveries.
- Delivery channels: secure S3 presigned uploads (preferred), SFTP, or an encrypted multipart over TLS. We will provide SHA256 checksums for each file and a top-level manifest.json (manifest will only contain filenames and checksums). If you require a signed chain-of-custody PDF, we can include export logs showing operator identity and export timestamps.
- Timeline: one-month sample within 5 business days after format confirmation; full 24-month scoped export 12–20 business days depending on scope and region.

Next steps I propose:
- Soojin: confirm delivery bucket or preferred method and procurement contact
- Emma: confirm you’re ok with hashed principal_id (HMAC-SHA256) and presigned S3
- Rishi/infra: once confirmed we’ll stage a one-month sample and attach checksums and manifest

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Platform Security, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachment(s): who_when_sample.csv, redwood_log_schema.md

Emma — thanks, and good notes. Confirming next steps and owners so procurement can greenlight:

1) Confirmed deliverable: one-month sample (NDJSON + CSV) with headers: event_id, timestamp_utc, model_name, endpoint_id, action_type, principal_type, principal_id_hmac, request_size_tokens, response_size_tokens, region, request_id. (Owner: Rishi; ETA: 5 business days)
2) Delivery method: presigned S3 upload from Redwood into your temporary upload bucket. Please send write-only ARN or presigned upload details to data-transfer@redwood.ai by EOD Monday. (Owner: Soojin / Monica)
3) Chain-of-custody checklist we’ll provide: exporter identity, SHA256 checksums, upload timestamp, manifest file with checksums. (Owner: Rishi)
4) DPA request: we will not start full 24-month export until we have a signed DPA addendum for the export and KMS/pseudonymization terms. I’ll coordinate legal touchpoints if procurement needs an initial template. (Owner: Soojin)

Action items for you (procurement/security):
- Confirm preferred delivery mechanism and send upload details
- Confirm acceptance of HMAC-SHA256 hashed principal_id (or request reversible pseudonymization)
- Share any additional fields you must have in the header for legal/procurement

I’ll prepare the one-month sample and include the manifest + checksums and a short README with how we generated principal_id_hmac. If you want a CSV-only sample first, tell me and we’ll prioritize that.

Best —
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
